layers.basics: A program stores values in variables, makes decisions with if/else, repeats with loops, and packages steps into functions.
layers.deeper: C is compiled ahead of time to machine code and leaves memory management to the programmer, which is why it is common in firmware. Python is interpreted: source is compiled to bytecode that a virtual machine runs, so each operation is slower, but programs are quick to write and suit analysis and test automation. C++ builds on C with classes, templates and automatic clean-up of resources (RAII).
layers.expert: Static vs dynamic typing; value vs reference semantics; stack frames; in C an array is a contiguous block of same-typed elements and a[i] means *(a+i); a Python list instead holds a contiguous array of references to separate objects.

title: The C language
summary: The lingua franca of hardware-near code.

layers.basics: C is a thin layer over the hardware: its types and pointers match what the machine does, but the compiler may heavily rewrite the code, and you manage memory yourself.
layers.deeper: Pointers, structs, bit operations and the preprocessor are the everyday tools of firmware developers.
layers.expert: Undefined behaviour (signed overflow, out-of-bounds access, strict-aliasing violations) lets the compiler assume it never happens, and it is one of the hazards that coding standards such as MISRA C, which aim at safety, security, portability and reliability in embedded code, try to rule out.

title: Data structures
summary: Lists, stacks, queues, trees, hash tables.

layers.basics: A data structure organises data so common operations are fast: arrays for indexing, linked lists for cheap insertion and removal once you hold a pointer to the spot (finding the spot still takes a walk through the list), trees for ordered search.
layers.deeper: Embedded code favours fixed-size ring buffers and state tables; simulators use sparse matrices.
layers.expert: Balanced search trees give O(log n) search, insert and delete; hash tables give O(1) average time per operation but O(n) in the worst case; appending to a dynamic array is amortised O(1). A fixed-size ring buffer is a common queue between an interrupt or DMA receiver and the main loop.

title: Algorithms, sorting and complexity
summary: How work grows with problem size.

layers.basics: Algorithms are recipes; complexity says how running time grows as inputs grow. Sorting is the classic example.
layers.deeper: FFT turns an O(N²) DFT into O(N log N), which is why spectrum analysers and OFDM radios are practical.
layers.expert: Big-O bounds growth from above, Ω from below and Θ from both sides. Any comparison sort must tell apart the n! possible orderings, and each comparison has two outcomes, so it needs at least log₂(n!) ≈ n log₂ n comparisons in the worst case, giving Ω(n log n); non-comparison sorts such as radix sort work differently and are not bound by this. Divide-and-conquer running times are analysed with the master theorem. Whether every problem whose answer can be checked in polynomial time can also be solved in polynomial time (P vs NP) is unresolved.

formula: T(n) = 2T(n/2) + Θ(n) ⇒ Θ(n log n)  (merge sort, radix-2 FFT: two half-size problems plus linear combine work)

layers.basics: Array-based languages make it easy to simulate signals and systems and to plot results.
layers.deeper: Scripts compute filter responses, FFTs and Monte Carlo noise studies; NumPy/SciPy and MATLAB cover much of the same numerical ground; MATLAB indexes from 1, NumPy from 0.
layers.expert: Vectorisation avoids interpreted loops; sparse and BLAS-backed linear algebra; toolboxes for control, signals and communications; reproducible notebooks.

title: Embedded C: pointers, memory, registers

layers.basics: In embedded C you write directly to hardware registers via pointers and often work with very little memory, from about a hundred bytes of RAM on the smallest 8-bit parts to many kilobytes on larger microcontrollers.
layers.deeper: Memory-mapped I/O, volatile, bit masks, interrupt service routines and linker scripts define the style.
layers.expert: The program image holds .text (code), .data (initialised globals, copied from flash to RAM at startup) and .bss (zero-initialised globals); the stack and heap are RAM regions managed at run time; volatile prevents optimisation of device reads; atomicity of shared variables between ISR and main loop; alignment and endianness.

formula: set bit n: REG |= (1u<<n);  clear bit n: REG &= ~(1u<<n)  (each is a non-atomic read-modify-write; not for write-1-to-clear registers)

ext.title: Wikipedia: Memory-mapped I/O and port-mapped I/O

layers.basics: An HDL describes digital hardware, not a sequence of steps: separate blocks and assignments operate concurrently, as real circuits do, although statements inside a single always block or process are evaluated in order.
layers.deeper: Synthesis tools turn the description into a netlist: lookup tables and flip-flops on an FPGA, or standard-cell gates on an ASIC; testbenches simulate it first.
layers.expert: Verilog RTL style: always @(posedge clk) with non-blocking (<=) assignments for registers, and assign or always @* with blocking (=) for combinational logic. In VHDL the equivalent is a clocked process using rising_edge(clk) with signals. An incomplete if or case in combinational code infers an unwanted latch; SystemVerilog assertions for verification.

layers.basics: Circuit simulators solve the circuit equations numerically so you can test a design before building it.
layers.deeper: SPICE-family simulators (the original Berkeley SPICE, LTspice, the SPICE engine in Multisim) model devices and run DC, AC, transient and noise analyses; Simulink instead simulates block-diagram systems.
layers.expert: Modified nodal analysis assembles one matrix of KCL equations; Newton–Raphson per timestep; device models (BSIM, Gummel–Poon) are only as good as their parameters. Field problems (COMSOL, HFSS) are handled by separate field solvers.

layers.basics: Field solvers discretise a structure (into finite elements, grid cells or surface patches) and solve Maxwell’s, heat or other field equations numerically.
layers.deeper: Used for antennas, PCB traces, magnetic cores and thermal design where closed forms do not exist.
layers.expert: Check that results stop changing as the mesh is refined. Excitation ports define how energy enters and leaves the model. A perfectly matched layer (PML) absorbs outgoing waves in open-region problems. FDTD is a time-domain grid method suited to wideband results, FEM handles complex geometry and materials, and the method of moments suits open metal structures such as wire antennas.
